newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: FIGURE SKATING-ISU IN HISTORIC DECISION OVER SCORING.
newsitem.headline: FIGURE SKATING-ISU IN HISTORIC DECISION OVER SCORING.

text.p: The International Skating Union (ISU) has ordered an immediate review of its judging system to find a way to make results more understandable to the public.

The move, described by the ISU as historic, is a result of confusion that surrounded the men's final at the European championships in Paris last month when Olympic champion Alexei Urmanov of Russia took the lead only after the final skater, who did not get among the medals, had finished.
"It is now time for a major review of the placing system," said ISU president Ottavio Cinquanta in a press release from the winter council meetings in Cape Town, South Africa last week.
"Figure skating is an extremely technical sport and it is not realistic to expect the public to be familiar with the complex but necessary rules.
"However, it is crucial that the public can easily understand how our sport is judged and we must develop a fair and comprehensible system."
Urmanov was second behind Viacheslav Zagorodniuk of Ukraine when the last skater, Andrei Vlascenko of Germany, began.
After he finished, Urmanov rose to first, Zagorodniuk dropped to third and Philippe Candeloro advanced two places to second. Vlascenko plunged from third to sixth.
The current judging system is based on placements of skaters in the short and free programmes of the event.

"The fact that millions of spectators at Bercy or watching on television did not understand the system of judging does not mean the system is wrong," Cinquanta told a news conference at the time. f"But it does mean the ISU must do something to ensure the spectators are not in that position again. It is time the ISU took the initiative to avoid this happening."

The ISU's figure skating and ice dance technical committees will conduct feasibility studies into alternative placing systems and submit a report to the ISU council at its next meeting in Prague in June.
